compare_record.reason: ROSCO_Helpers.f90:325 (clean baseline 54dd134) PRINTs a warning record naming the variable and the default value it substituted -- `PRINT *, "ROSCO Warning: Did not find "//TRIM(VarName)//" in input file.  Using default value of ", TRIM(Variable)`. It is the only thing that tells a ROSCO user their input file did not supply the value, and it crosses no dummy argument, so R4 never named it and no no_oracle could have excluded it: the exclusion was structural rather than a judgement anybody made. Unit #55 measured what that costs -- five of its six surviving mutants edited its own record and nothing else -- and units #56, #57 and this one take the comparison at their first dispatch instead of at a sixth. The record is TWO ADJACENT CHARACTER ITEMS, a layout no unit in this family has had: #55 writes CHARACTER, an array of integers, then a CHARACTER; #56 writes CHARACTER then one REAL; #57 writes CHARACTER then one INTEGER. So it turns on the one libgfortran rule none of them exercised -- a CHARACTER item following a CHARACTER item takes NO separator when DELIM=NONE, which is the default -- and that rule was derived from libgfortran's own list_formatted_write_scalar and then priced against gfortran's record before the corpus was generated: evidence/ParseInput_Str_Opt/print_record_probe.{f90,cpp,txt}, 9 of 9 byte-identical across item lengths 0, 1, 5, 6, 7, 256 and 1024, which straddle the truncation of the six-byte default.
